[01:35] Nina Park: and from legal, the DPA redlines include a clause for deletion on request plus audit rights. also we need SOC2 or equivalent attestation and breach notification timing spelled out.

[02:20] Marta Ruiz: can you send that now? procurement will attach it to the intake form.

[02:33] Liam Ortega: yes i'll drop it in the shared link.

[03:00] Priya Nair: diving into deployment options — Redwood Private = private control plane in your VPC, full KMS/HSM integration, customer-managed networking. Redwood Dedicate (sic) is our reserved pool option with tenant isolation; hosted API is fastest but doesn't support customer keying or guaranteed region pinning.

[03:35] Ethan Cole: when you say KMS integration, do you support an HSM-backed key wrap and envelope encryption? or is it only KMS API calls?

[03:50] Priya Nair: we support both envelope encryption with customer keys and HSM-backed wrappers through our KMS provider integrations. there might be some ops work for on-prem HSMs — we'll document the runbook.

[04:10] Marta Ruiz: about the MSA: we marked three redline areas — liability cap, data processing scope, and a clause around model outputs being non-infringing. can you speak to your standard positions?

[04:30] Liam Ortega: on liability, standard is a contract cap around fees paid in 12 months; enterprise exceptions can be scoped. for DPA, we can accept narrow processing purpose language, and for model output indemnity — that one is tricky; we usually limit to willful misconduct and where we control model weights.

[05:05] Nina Park: ok legal will need a stronger assurance around model lineage; Veridian can't accept vague language that says 'we tried our best'. we need traceability for model version and for any third-party model provenance.

[05:35] Priya Nair: actionable option: we can pin the pilot to a specific open model and provide a signed manifest with the model hash and version. also Redwood Console (we'll call it console) keeps per-request metadata and model version tagging that you can export for audits.

[06:05] Ethan Cole: is that export cryptographically verifiable? like signed logs?

[06:15] Priya Nair: we provide append-only audit logs and can integrate with your SIEM. signing of logs is on the roadmap; current approach is tamper-evident storage plus chain-of-custody metadata.

[06:35] Marta Ruiz: latency and cost — procurement wants to understand the delta between hosted and dedicated for our typical query patterns. we saw a competitor quote that was cheaper but had higher p95 latency.

[06:55] Liam Ortega: we'll provide a pricing band. rough rule: hosted = lowest operational lift, variable unit pricing; dedicated = predictable throughput, lower unit cost at scale but commit; private = higher setup cost, predictable TCO for regulated data. we will include a simple cost-per-100k-tokens model in the pricing sheet we send.

[07:30] Speaker 6: (inaudible)

[07:40] Priya Nair: for benchmarks, we propose three tests for the pilot: 1) p50/p95 latency for 32-64 token completions, 2) sustained throughput with batching at 16 concurrent streams, 3) cold-start KV cache hit/miss behavior. i'll own the test plan.

[08:05] Ethan Cole: KV cash? sorry, i meant KV cache — we've seen poor cold-starts elsewhere.

[08:15] Priya Nair: yep kv cache, sorry pronounced. we'll show both warm and cold time series. also quantization profiles can change latency — we'll include model-quantization notes.

[08:40] Nina Park: on data retention and deletion, DPA redline asks for deletion within 30 days of request. is that doable?

[08:55] Liam Ortega: yes, for Redwood Private and Dedicated we can offer configurable retention windows; hosted has standard retention but we do offer short retention enterprise settings. the deletion flow: data marked for deletion, purge job, and audit log entry.

[09:20] Marta Ruiz: what about infra egress? we can't accept cross-border processing. all inference must stay in us-east-1. can you promise region pinning?

[09:40] Priya Nair: yes, region pinning is supported for Private and for Dedicated pools in us-east-1. hosted global endpoints may route to nearest region by default, but we can set policy-based routing for your account.

[10:00] Ethan Cole: encryption in transit — do you support mutually authenticated TLS or mTLS?

[10:10] Priya Nair: mTLS is supported for private deployments; for hosted we support TLS with client certs for certain enterprise arrangements. we'll include specifics in the runbook.

[10:35] Liam Ortega: quick pause — i want to call out that we've had customers ask for embargoed access to model weights; if you need that, it's a different engagement but we can discuss.

[10:55] Nina Park: not for now, but good to know. legal will want the MSA to call out who owns model outputs specifically.

[11:22] Priya Nair: we support SAML and SCIM for provisioning; we can map roles to RBAC in the console.

[11:40] Ethan Cole: monitoring — we need token-level cost reporting and per-route latency dashboards. does your console show per-route breakouts?

[11:50] Priya Nair: yes per-route, model, and token-level breakdowns are available; retention for logs is configurable per tier.

[12:05] Marta Ruiz: procurement need: sample SLA with uptime, p95 latency SLOs, and credits. what do you usually offer?

[12:20] Liam Ortega: standard enterprise SLA is 99.9% for Dedicated, with p95 latency targets dependent on model and sequence length. credits for missed SLOs scale by severity. we can provide the SLA matrix for pilot model variants.

[12:50] Nina Park: small ask — can you commit to a 48-hour breach notification window in the MSA?

[12:58] Liam Ortega: yes we can accept 48 hours for confirmed incidents; for suspected incidents we usually notify within 72 hours while we investigate. we'll mark that for redlines.

[13:20] Marta Ruiz: pricing approvals — procurement has two tiers of approvers. finance will want an annualized TCO estimate comparing hosted vs dedicated vs private. can you provide that spreadsheet?

[13:40] Liam Ortega: we'll send TCO v1 with assumptions and sensitivity. if you have query volumes, send them and we'll tailor it.

[14:05] Ethan Cole: about penetration testing and attestation — do you allow third-party pen tests on Private deployments?

[14:15] Priya Nair: on Private yes, subject to scheduling and an NDA; for Hosted we do periodic pen tests and can share summary reports.

[14:40] Marta Ruiz: ok that's important.

[15:00] Priya Nair: back to technical: for the pilot we recommend a small Dedicated pool pinned to us-east-1 with model quantized to int8 for cost-savings and a prefix cache for common completions. this gives you predictable latency and cost.

[15:25] Ethan Cole: any fallback if Dedicated capacity is under pressure?

[15:33] Priya Nair: yes we support automated fallback policies — route to a compatible model variant or spill to hosted with data policy guards. you can set strict no-fallback if that suits.

[15:55] Nina Park: legal question: fallback to hosted implies data leaving your intended environment; how is that addressed in the DPA?

[16:05] Liam Ortega: fallback is conditional and only with your explicit policy. default pilot policy will be no-fallback; we surface the option in the Console and in the policy config.
